dedupe_keys.name: canadian institute for cybersecurity cic university of new brunswick datasets network iot ev charger and substation attack captures

description: The Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity at the University of New Brunswick publishes a collection of labelled cybersecurity datasets that are widely used to train and test intrusion and anomaly detection. The index page groups them into IoT sets (for example Datasense IIoT 2025, CICIoMT2024, CICIoV2024 and the EVSE charger set of 2024), DNS sets, intrusion detection sets (CIC-IDS 2017, CSE-CIC-IDS 2018, CIC-DDoS 2019, CICEV 2023 and the older ISCX sets), malware, phishing and an operational technology set, Modbus 2023. Coverage: laboratory and testbed captures. The Modbus 2023 set holds packet captures and attack logs from a simulated substation network of IEDs and SCADA HMIs in Docker, with reconnaissance, flooding, false data injection, replay and other attacks based on MITRE ICS ATT&CK; the EVSE 2024 set records power use, network traffic and host activity of a Level 2 charging station under benign and attack conditions. Format and access: PCAP captures and CSV logs and features, downloaded from each dataset page; free. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): set per dataset on each dataset page (e.g. CIC Modbus 2023: redistribution allowed with citation). Caveats: most sets are generated in labs, so traffic mixes and attack rates are not those of real operations; PCAP timestamps in Modbus 2023 are in Atlantic Daylight Time while logs are in UTC. Simulation uses: training and testing detection of cyber attacks on substations, charging stations and connected vehicles for resilience and cascading failure studies. Related records: SANDI-2024 (data-sandi-2024-substation-intrusion-detection) and the IEC 104 SCADA set (data-iec104-scada-ids-dataset) are other substation intrusion sets.
